name: eventsStream
description: Server sent events. Each event is sent as `event: ordex-event` with `id: <sequence>:<eventId>`: the envelope sequence and id, so the id both names the event and is its exact resume position without any lookup. Sending that id back as Last-Event-ID (or as the cursor query parameter) resumes exactly after the event. A cursor older than the retained window answers 410 CURSOR_EXPIRED before any event, and the client resyncs instead of skipping events. Sequences are counted per network. On a stream filtered to one network the resume is exact. On a stream with no network filter, a <sequence>:<eventId> position is exact for that event's network, and the other networks restart from their oldest retained event: the consumer receives duplicates, which it drops by event id, and never a gap. A consumer that needs an exact resume across networks opens one stream per network. Filters: network, type, aggregateType, aggregateId, protocol, collectionId.

heartbeat.description: A comment line at least every 15 seconds so proxies never close an idle stream.

name: eventsSocket
description: WebSocket for high volume consumers. One connection carries up to 16 subscriptions, each named by a client chosen id. Every server frame is JSON with an op field; events arrive wrapped as {op: event, id, cursor, event} so each subscription resumes from its own cursor. Buffers are bounded; a slow consumer gets a disconnect frame carrying every subscription's cursor, then the socket closes with code 4008.

name: webhookDelivery
description: HTTP POST of one envelope per delivery, signed with the X-Ordex-Signature header: t=<unix>,d=<deliveryId>,v1=<hmac-sha256 over timestamp.deliveryId.sha256(body)>. Verify with the SDK enforcer or verifier/events.js.
